answers.value: ASC 730-10-50-1 requires disclosure of the total R&D costs charged to expense in each income statement period presented. R&D costs are expensed as incurred and reported as an operating expense; the total (here $1,778,000.00 for Year 1) is disclosed either as a separate line item on the face of the income statement or in the notes/significant accounting policies, and includes depreciation of capitalized multi-use assets used in R&D.

journal_entries.description: Item 1 - Materials consumed on current R&D projects (no alternative future use) (expensed as R&D when incurred)
Item 2 - Laboratory equipment (significant alternative future uses) (capitalized: alternative future use)
Item 3 - Specialized testing apparatus, single project, no alternative use (expensed as R&D when incurred)
Item 4 - Salaries and wages of R&D scientists and technicians (expensed as R&D when incurred)
Item 5 - Contract research fees paid to outside university lab (expensed as R&D when incurred)
Item 6 - Reasonable allocation of indirect facility costs related to R&D (expensed as R&D when incurred)
Item 7 - Corporate headquarters G&A not clearly related to R&D (not R&D)
Item 8 - Troubleshooting/repair of existing commercial production line (not R&D; routine production cost)
Item 9 - Design and construction of preproduction prototypes (expensed as R&D when incurred)
Item 10 - Legal fees to register patent on successfully developed process (capitalized registration cost, not R&D)
Summary of part a: total R&D expensed immediately vs capitalized vs non-R&D
Dec 31, Year 1 - depreciation of multi-use laboratory equipment (charged to R&D)
Dec 31, Year 1 - patent amortization (6 months, not R&D)
Jan 1, Year 4 - sale of multi-use laboratory equipment for cash

notes: Item 2 equipment has alternative future uses, so it is capitalized and only its annual straight-line depreciation ($480,000/6 = $80,000) is charged to R&D expense; item 3 apparatus has no alternative future use, so its full $96,000 is expensed immediately as R&D even though purchased April 1 (no depreciation on it). Items 7 (corporate G&A) and 8 (routine troubleshooting/repair of an existing commercial production line) are not R&D under ASC 730-10-55. Item 9 preproduction prototypes ARE R&D. Item 10 patent registration legal fees are capitalized as an intangible (not R&D) and amortized over the shorter 10-year useful life from July 1, Year 1 ($600 in Year 1); patent amortization is not part of R&D expense. Year 1 R&D disclosure = 240,000 + 96,000 + 1,150,000 + 85,000 + 72,000 + 55,000 + 80,000 = 1,778,000. Sale on Jan 1, Year 4: book value 480,000 - 240,000 = 240,000 vs proceeds 250,000, so a 10,000 gain (no Year 4 depreciation because the sale is on the first day of the year).
